text_en: At the bend beyond the shrine, the sign is lying where nobody can read it without leaving the road.
That is an unhelpful place for a helpful thing.
The post is loose. I can stand it up again.
Wait. We should see why it fell.
A sign that tells us to step off the path deserves a little suspicion.
There are tracks behind it. Not all of them came from the road.
Something is moving at the far bend.
Brin turns the sign face-up without pushing it into the earth.
We clear the passage before anyone follows it.
The footing is soft here.
I can find where it stops being soft.
I can keep it steady while you look.
Set it down until we have chosen the place. You do not need to hold it for us to talk.
Brin lowers the post. Nothing important falls with it.
A useful beginning.
I was afraid the plan would involve all of us leaning against it until evening.
That would be a bad plan.
I can read the turn first. Find what is coming and where it can reach.
Or we brace the narrow side. Give the people behind us a clear place to wait.
Either can work. Tell us what you need from the rest of us.
Preferably before we all volunteer for the same end of a post.
Stay where you can see the sign. I will not go beyond the first tree.
I will watch the space behind you.
Call before you need us to move.
We need a solid footing, not a taller barrier.
I will check both approaches while you choose it.
Then neither of you has to watch everything.
See the leaves along the edge? Something crossed the soft ground after they fell.
A heavy step?
A dragging one. And this mark keeps going after the turn.
We can read that part without following it.
What else do you hear?
A faint knock comes from behind the bend. It does not follow the wind.
Enough to choose what we watch first.
The track tells us where something can reach. The knock tells us where the dead turn together.
We can prepare for one first, without forgetting the other.
Choose it. We stay within sight.
The dragging staff can reach around the front. Keep the rear where we can protect it.
I can hold the nearest one while you choose the attacker.
Then I will stay where both of you can see me.
The knock comes before the others move. We will see the bellbound one as soon as we step out.
A target to notice. Not a reason to chase without checking the lane.
I will keep the space behind us clear.
Here. They can see it before the turn.
Not where you were standing when you drew it.
You checked it from the other side.
That is where someone will need it.
A map improved by having more than one pair of feet.
We have the observation. Now we clear the passage.
The bank is firm. The beam is dry underneath.
The narrow side is open from both. We can see the turn.
Which place lets you share the work?
Either, if someone watches the side I cannot.
We can do that.
Brin tests the ground once more, then steps back far enough for Nixie to see it too.
The bank leaves a wide place behind us. The beam keeps the narrow line straight.
If we use the bank, I can watch farther across. If we use the beam, I can watch the near gap.
Both keep the road open. Choose the line you want to hold.
Then we hold where nobody has to crowd behind me.
I will watch across the opening. Call if you need the pressure off one side.
I will.
The beam gives us a straight line. Nobody stands on it.
I will watch the gap beside it. The support behind the dead is visible from here.
A useful beam, with no volunteers underneath it.
I can keep this side clear.
Then I will check the other side.
Call if you need me.
You too.
Brin nods as if it is an instruction worth remembering.
Good. We move together when the line is ready.
The first dead figure appears around the bend. A staff strikes the post and keeps dragging.
There. The others are behind it.
We have space. Keep it.
The road is clear behind us.
Look at their intentions before choosing the first target.
The fallen sign stays face-up, outside the fighting ground.
Steady now.
And the arrow points before the turn.
I will check the far side one more time.
We have built a very small thing with a great deal of advice.
It only has to be useful.
Nixie reads it from the road. Brin lets go of the post. It stays where it was put.
Useful from this side too.
Is the turn clear?
Yes. Follow the mark before the bend. The sign is facing you now.
I was waiting for somebody else to take it first.
You can take your time.
Do you need my name for the register?
The shrine keeper can help you with the register. We are clearing the road.
Then I will give it there.
A sensible place to stop.
The traveler tests the footing, then walks through without needing to hurry.
They did not ask which way again.
They could see it.
That is a useful kind of answer.
We should continue before the road grows busy.
It is allowed to grow busy. That is what we fixed it for.
Mahmut looks at the path, then nods. They gather their things without taking down the sign.
The post no longer needs a shoulder. The company has one quiet moment before moving on.
It stayed when you let go.
We chose the ground before I held it.
That was a very good improvement to the plan.
You watched the side I could not.
And you both told us where to stand.
Brin checks the post once with her hand, not her whole weight.
Brin saw the mark from where the traveler would need it.
You drew it where it could be seen.
After you looked.
An arrow with a second opinion. We should keep the idea.
We can use it at the next turn.
Nixie leaves the chalk in her pouch. This mark does not need another correction.
Ready?
Ready.
Good. I was beginning to think the sign might join the company.
It has a place to stay.
Behind them, the road bends out of sight. The arrow points before it does.
